clue.text: In going before board, unionist revolutionary shows defiance of authority

indicators.note: going before says the word In is placed at the front of what follows
revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters of board and unionist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade unionist radical marches into a boardroom meeting in open revolt against the management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as describing the unionist, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it; 'shows' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey superiors is exactly a refusal to submit, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Independent agreements encompassing mass strikes

indicators.note: encompassing means the first pieces surround the letter for mass

parts.note: pacts are agreements or treaties
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Independent trade agreements that cover mass industrial strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The M sits between the I and PACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns, strikes and collisions are both blows landing forcefully, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Teams with spin bowlers all out bar the tail-ender

parts.note: in snooker and billiards, side is spin put on the ball

indicators.note: every letter of bowlers goes out except the one at the tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: Cricket teams with spin bowlers are all dismissed except the last batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'all out' and 'tail-ender' (a weak late batsman) set the scene; here they mean only the last letter of 'bowlers' stays. Side is the billiards word for spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports teams are commonly called sides, especially in British usage.

clue.text: Part of car was very hot around front of radiator — strange!

indicators.note: around means the phrase for very hot surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: baked means sweltered, was very hot

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of radiator

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A car part ran very hot near the radiator, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' looks like a comment on the overheating, but rum is old British slang for odd and supplies the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This drum-shaped wheel component of a vehicle's braking system is a car part.

clue.text: No one is up supporting double-crosser getting allowance

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed beneath, so this part comes after

parts.note: a rat is a traitor who betrays his allies

indicators.note: in a down clue is up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nobody backs a traitor who wants a share of the allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No one' looks like nobody, but it splits into the word no plus I for one, and in a down clue 'is up' reads them bottom to top to make ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed portion or quota allowed to each person, as in wartime food, is a ration.

clue.text: Courageous international agent needs passport, for example

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
a passport is an example of identification, ID

explanation.surface: A brave spy working abroad needs a passport.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and bold, the word is a direct synonym for brave.

clue.text: Nearly open for a drink?

parts.note: jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A pub nearly open for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a jar' is British slang for a pint of beer, so 'a drink' gives A JAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is described this way, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Involve mischievous child with tall story about pet

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child

indicators.note: about means the word for tall story goes around the pet

parts.note: a lie is an untrue tale, a tall story
a cat is a typical pet

explanation.surface: Drag a naughty youngster into it, with some fib about the family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag someone into a crime or affair is to involve them in it.

clue.text: Wanted to cross line, annoyed

indicators.note: to cross here means to lie across, the word for wanted holding the letter for line

parts.note: needed means wanted or required

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to cross the picket line and grew irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be irritated or provoked, a direct synonym.

clue.text: School actors for internet service

parts.note: a pod is a group, or school, of whales or dolphins
the cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A drama school's actors put on a show for an online broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio programme you download or stream online is a service delivered through the web.

clue.text: Tyre, oddly, has more than enough tread

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of Tyre

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A tyre, strangely, has plenty of tread left on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tread' looks like the noun on a tyre, but here it is the verb to walk heavily on.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread heavily over something, crushing it underfoot, is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bad loser in lawsuit is a dish

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit inside the word for lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit brought before a court

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of loser are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sore loser in a court case is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad loser' reads as a poor sport, but 'Bad' is the anagram signal and yields SEROL; 'is a' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-cooked stew, named after the pot it is cooked in, is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Determination of women suffering

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
ill means unwell, suffering

explanation.surface: The determination shown by women who are suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve or strength of purpose is willpower, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Excellent, for each will be protected by advance on wages

indicators.note: will be protected by means the word for each goes inside the advance

parts.note: a sub is British slang for a loan against pay
per means for each

explanation.surface: Each worker is covered by an advance on their pay, which is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: A sub is British slang for a payment ahead of wages.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate or superb in quality, the adjective is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Top up and serve half of rich smorgasbord

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: to pour drinks is to serve them

indicators.note: half of takes the first two letters of rich

explanation.surface: Top up the glasses and dish out half of a rich buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top up' looks like refilling but means TOP read upwards, giving POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a varied mixture or miscellany of things, figurative synonyms.

clue.text: Magazine rejected hotel — a case of rancid fish

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for magazine reads backwards

parts.note: a clip is a gun's ammunition magazine
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: case of takes the outside letters of rancid

explanation.surface: A magazine rejected a hotel review after a plate of rancid fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' is a gun clip, not a publication. Reversed it gives PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, related to the sardine.

clue.text: Made up arguments against planned diets

parts.note: cons are arguments against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters of diets are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Fabricated objections to carefully planned diets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges DIETS into ISTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up in the sense of composed of, as in a meal comprising three courses.

clue.text: Loudly assertive step, clamping down on National Trust

indicators.note: in a down clue clamping down on puts this word on top of the next piece

parts.note: a stride is a long step
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A noisy, pushy move to crack down on the National Trust.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, forceful voice or campaigner is described as strident, a synonym.

clue.text: Close friend of prisoner hiding note

indicators.note: hiding means the word for prisoner wraps around the note

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A prisoner's close friend is hiding a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message, but it is the musical note TI.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a confidant or very close companion is an intimate.

clue.text: Zinc is organic, offering something with bite

indicators.note: offering means the phrase gives up letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: Zinc in organic form gives a product some bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting front tooth is literally used for biting, so a playful description.

clue.text: French city does annoy

definitions.meaning: a city on the Loire in western France

explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Loire is spelt the same as the verb meaning irritates.

clue.text: Transfixes second people in line for broadcast

indicators.note: for broadcast means the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: those waiting in a queue are queuers

explanation.surface: A broadcast instantly grips a queue of people.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEUERS spoken sounds like KEWERS, which follows S.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce right through with a spike is to transfix, as with meat on a kebab.

clue.text: Complaint from motoring organisation about street followed by Her Majesty

indicators.note: about means the motoring organisation goes around the next pieces

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: followed by means the abbreviation for street comes first and Her Majesty after

explanation.surface: A complaint from a motoring club about a road named after the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Automobile Association) is Britain's best-known roadside rescue club; 'Complaint' is an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: In medical usage a complaint is an ailment, and this breathing condition is one.

clue.text: Work on carbon monoxide compound

indicators.note: on means the word for work is placed after the formula

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A chemist works on a compound of carbon monoxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks chemical but is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure or pen for poultry is a kind of compound.

clue.text: To start off, it's roughly covered by home attendance

indicators.note: covered by means the rearranged letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means at home
the gate is the number of spectators attending a match

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters of the word are arranged loosely

explanation.surface: To kick things off, the home crowd is a rough estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' seems to mean approximately, but it rearranges it's into STI; 'covered by' then places that inside the two other pieces. Gate is the British term for a match crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or initiate something is to set it in motion, a synonym.

clue.text: Nice friend shot mate from Spain

parts.note: in Nice, a city in France, a friend is ami
a go is an attempt, a shot

explanation.surface: A pleasant friend shot a Spanish companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is not pleasant but the French city, so its word for friend is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend or companion, often used in English too.

clue.text: Oddly, team lick white powder

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Strangely, the team lick a white powder.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft mineral, ground fine, is sold as a white powder for skin.

clue.text: Top expert on breakers

indicators.note: on means the expert comes after the word for breakers

parts.note: breakers are waves, the surf
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A top expert at riding the breaking waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the expert but is the definition, the noun for an outer face.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper or outer layer of something is its top, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Popular range giving link to president?

parts.note: hot means in demand, popular
a line is a range of products

explanation.surface: A popular product range offers a link to the company president.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition evokes the Cold War direct phone link between Washington and Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct phone connection between heads of state, famously between Washington and the Kremlin.

clue.text: Come down heavily on addicts as gran gets trashed

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandmother cracks down hard on drug addicts and ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down heavily on' looks like a phrase, but 'on' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes very heavy rainfall, so it means to pour down.
